lessons.title: Work, energy and power
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Physics — Work, energy, power, machines, energy sources (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Define work, energy and power with their units.
Calculate work done W = Fd, kinetic energy ½mv², potential energy mgh and power P = W/t.
Compare renewable and non-renewable energy sources.
reviewNotes: Statements about Cameroon's electricity (a large share from hydroelectric dams such as those on the Sanaga) are general; no percentages given.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Work, energy, power
blocks.md: **Work** is done when a force moves an object: $W = Fd$ (d in the direction of the force). **Energy** is the ability to do work; both are measured in **joules (J)**. **Power** is the rate of doing work: $P = \frac{W}{t}$, in **watts (W)** (1 W = 1 J/s; 1 kW = 1000 W).

blocks.title: Mechanical energy
blocks.md:
- **Kinetic energy** (movement): $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$
- **Gravitational potential energy** (height): $E_p = mgh$ (g = 10 N/kg)

**Conservation of energy**: energy is never created or destroyed; it is changed from one form to another. If friction is ignored, the total of $E_k + E_p$ stays constant.

blocks.title: Energy sources
blocks.md: **Non-renewable**: coal, oil and natural gas (fossil fuels), which run out. **Renewable**: hydroelectric (water), solar, wind, biomass (wood, biogas). Much electricity in Cameroon is generated from water flowing through hydroelectric dams; solar panels are common in sunny regions. Fossil fuels release carbon dioxide when burnt.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.md:
- Work needs movement: holding a heavy bag still does no work (in physics).
- Doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy **four** times bigger (v is squared).
- Use the vertical height for potential energy, not the length of a slope.

blocks.caption: A ball falling: potential energy changes into kinetic energy.
blocks.alt: A vertical line with three balls, at the top (all potential energy), half way (half and half) and at the bottom (all kinetic energy).

blocks.title: Example 1 — pushing a handcart
blocks.statement: A man pushes a handcart with a force of 150 N over 40 m in 50 s. Find the work done and his power.

blocks.title: Example 2 — falling ball
blocks.statement: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m (g = 10 N/kg, no air resistance). Find the speed when it reaches the ground.
steps: Potential energy at the top = mgh = 0.5 × 10 × 20 = 100 J.
At the bottom all of it is kinetic: ½mv² = 100, so 0.25 v² = 100 and v² = 400.

lessons.title: Simple machines and efficiency
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Physics — Work, energy, power, machines, energy sources (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Describe levers, pulleys and inclined planes.
Define mechanical advantage (MA), velocity ratio (VR) and efficiency.
Calculate efficiency from work done or from MA/VR.
Explain why no machine is 100% efficient.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: MA, VR and efficiency
blocks.md:
A **machine** makes work easier by changing the size or direction of a force.

- **Mechanical advantage** MA = load ÷ effort (no unit).
- **Velocity ratio** VR = distance moved by effort ÷ distance moved by load.
- **Efficiency** = (work output ÷ work input) × 100% = (MA ÷ VR) × 100%.

blocks.title: Common machines
blocks.md:
- **Lever**: a rigid bar turning about a pivot (crowbar, wheelbarrow, scissors); based on moments.
- **Pulley system**: for a frictionless system VR = number of rope sections supporting the load.
- **Inclined plane (ramp)**: VR = length of slope ÷ vertical height.
- A machine can multiply force but never energy.

blocks.title: Why efficiency is below 100%
blocks.md: Some input energy is always wasted as heat (friction) and in lifting the moving parts of the machine. So work output < work input, MA < VR and efficiency < 100%. Oiling the moving parts improves efficiency.

blocks.caption: An inclined plane (ramp): a crate is pushed up a 5 m slope to a height of 2 m.
blocks.alt: A right-angled triangle ramp with a crate on the slope, an effort arrow pointing up the slope, slope length 5 m and height 2 m.

blocks.title: Example 1 — pulley
blocks.statement: An effort of 150 N lifts a load of 400 N using a pulley system with VR = 4. Find the MA and the efficiency.

blocks.title: Example 2 — ramp
blocks.statement: A crate of weight 500 N is pushed up a ramp 5 m long by an effort of 250 N parallel to the slope. The ramp's top is 2 m above the ground. Find the efficiency.
steps: Work input = effort × distance along the slope = 250 × 5 = 1250 J.
Work output = load × vertical height = 500 × 2 = 1000 J.
